title: A proper homogeneous ideal admits a graded-field quotient
statement: Let $M$ be an abelian group written additively and $A$ a commutative ring with additive subgroups $A_n$ such that every element has a unique finite homogeneous expansion, $1\in A_0$, and $A_nA_r\subseteq A_{n+r}$. Call an ideal homogeneous if it contains every homogeneous component of each of its elements. For every proper homogeneous ideal $L\subsetneq A$ there is a proper homogeneous ideal $H$ containing $L$, maximal among proper homogeneous ideals. The quotient ring $D=A/H$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], with quotient map $q:A\to D$, is nonzero and is graded by $D_n=q(A_n)$. Every nonzero $d\in D_n$ has an inverse $e\in D_{-n}$ with $de=1$.

source.place: Tag 00JM (section-proj), opening definition of homogeneous ideals, generalized from the displayed grading to an arbitrary abelian group. The maximal homogeneous quotient and inverse assertion are agent-written auxiliary results; their complete Zorn argument is retained in the Q112 report, not asserted to be a theorem of 00JM.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal S$ be the set of proper homogeneous ideals of $A$ containing $L$, ordered by inclusion. It contains $L$. For a nonempty chain $\mathcal C$, its union $U$ is an ideal: any two elements lie in a common member, where subtraction and multiplication by $A$ preserve membership. Each component of an element of $U$ lies in that same member, so $U$ is homogeneous. It contains $L$ and is proper, since $1\in U$ would imply $1$ belongs to a proper member. The empty chain has upper bound $L$.

source.place: Tag 00JM (section-proj), opening componentwise definition of homogeneous ideals; agent-written argument for arbitrary abelian group gradings, retained in coord/reports/Q112/lem-sfb-graded-stabilizer-strong-products.md, Complete proof retained for the new node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zorn-lemma] with $X=A$ and the family $\mathcal S$ of step 1. Every chain, including the empty chain, has an upper bound in $\mathcal S$. Obtain a maximal member $H$. Any proper homogeneous ideal containing $H$ also contains $L$, hence belongs to $\mathcal S$ and equals $H$. This is the required maximality among proper homogeneous ideals.

source.place: Tag 00JM (section-proj), opening componentwise definition of homogeneous ideals; agent-written argument for arbitrary abelian group gradings, retained in coord/reports/Q112/lem-sfb-graded-stabilizer-strong-products.md, Complete proof retained for the new node.

proof.text: Use [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] to form the surjective ring map $q:A\to D=A/H$ with kernel $H$. Put $D_r=q(A_r)$, additive subgroups. Surjectivity and the finite homogeneous expansions in $A$ show they span $D$. For distinct degrees $r$ and lifts $a_r\in A_r$, the relation $\sum_r q(a_r)=0$ implies $\sum_r a_r\in H$; homogeneity then gives $a_r\in H$ for each $r$. Thus all $q(a_r)=0$, proving uniqueness of the finite expansion in $D$. Also $1_D=q(1)\in D_0$ and $D_rD_s\subseteq D_{r+s}$. Since $1\notin H=\ker q$, $1_D\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 00JM (section-proj), opening componentwise definition of homogeneous ideals; agent-written argument for arbitrary abelian group gradings, retained in coord/reports/Q112/lem-sfb-graded-stabilizer-strong-products.md, Complete proof retained for the new node.

proof.text: Fix $0\ne d\in D_n$ and lift it to $a\in A_n$. Then $a\notin H$. The set $J=H+(a)=\{h+ax:h\in H,\ x\in A\}$ is an ideal: it is closed under subtraction and multiplication by any element of $A$. For every $r\in M$, the degree-$r$ component of $h+ax$ is $h_r+a x_{r-n}$. Indeed, multiplication sends the finite expansion of $x$ to degrees $n+s$, which are distinct because translation by $n$ in $M$ is injective. Since $h_r\in H$, every component belongs to $J$, so $J$ is homogeneous. It strictly contains $H$ because $a\in J\setminus H$. Thus maximality of $H$ forces $J=A$.

source.place: Tag 00JM (section-proj), opening componentwise definition of homogeneous ideals; agent-written argument for arbitrary abelian group gradings, retained in coord/reports/Q112/lem-sfb-graded-stabilizer-strong-products.md, Complete proof retained for the new node.

proof.text: Write $1=h+ax$ with $h\in H$ and $x\in A$, using $J=A$. Taking the degree-zero component of this equality gives $1=h_0+a x_{-n}$, with $h_0\in H$. The quotient map therefore satisfies $1_D=q(a)q(x_{-n})=d q(x_{-n})$. Set $e=q(x_{-n})\in D_{-n}$. Then $de=1_D$ as required (and $ed=1_D$ by commutativity).
